lines.text: No mouth. No stomach. No gut at all.
And a grown one stands up to about two metres tall.
It was found in 1977, two and a half kilometres down, near the Galápagos Islands, by the submersible Alvin.
Its home is a crack in the sea floor, where the water comes out of the rock at more than seven hundred degrees Fahrenheit.
No sunlight has ever reached this place. And a grown worm never eats at all.
And it wasn't alone. The same discovery turned up clams a foot long.
So what is feeding all of them — in a place the Sun has never touched?
The answer is level six of the full dive, linked right here.
